subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which remaining direct-invoke surfaces should OpenClaw core support beyond the shipped HTTP/RPC/SDK and command-cron paths, and what owner/security gates are required for each?
rationale: The unresolved work can expose filesystem, process, session, Gateway, cron, and node actions without a model turn, so automation cannot safely choose the supported product boundary or security gate shape.

options.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
options.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing the active direct-invoke PRs, requiring explicit owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Limit support to shipped paths
options.body: Declare HTTP/RPC/SDK direct invoke and command cron sufficient for now, and reject host-FS, exec, slash, and CLI direct dispatch until a new maintainer-sponsored proposal exists.

options.title: Approve broader direct execution
options.body: Allow broader direct execution only with a named security design, compatibility plan, and operator-facing controls that make the risk explicit.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing the active direct-invoke PRs, requiring explicit owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily the dangerous-tool and owner-gated Gateway security boundary, where recent history points to Peter Steinberger as the strongest routing candidate.
